study_identification_part.si_4_title: Brain-Charting Autism and Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder Reveals Distinct and Overlapping Neurobiology

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: The study used Generalized Additive Models for Location Scale and Shape (GAMLSS) to generate reference normative models from a sample of 75,241 typically developing individuals, mapping neuroanatomical developmental trajectories across the lifespan. Out-of-sample centile scores were generated for the study sample using Brent's maximum likelihood estimation. The GAMLSS models were originally developed in Bethlehem et al. (2022) Brain Charts paper. Sex-stratified GAMLSS models estimated first-order (μ) and second-order (σ) distribution parameters of a generalised gamma distribution using fractional polynomials to model nonlinear trends.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: Our previous work (98) generated reference models using generalized additive models of location scale and shape to map neuroanatomical developmental trajectories across the life span, using a sample of 75,241 TD individuals; Adopting a sex-stratified approach, the GAMLSS model included age, preprocessing pipeline, and study in estimating firstorder (μ) and second-order (σ) distribution parameters of a generalised gamma distribution using fractional polynomials to model nonlinear trends.

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: The study modeled multiple structural MRI measures: total gray matter volume (GMV), subcortical gray matter volume (sGMV), white matter volume (WMV), ventricular volume (CSF), total surface area (SA), mean cortical thickness (CT), regional cortical thickness, regional cortical volume (CV), and regional surface area. Regional measures were extracted based on the Desikan-Killiany atlas and averaged across hemispheres. T1-weighted scans from FreeSurfer version 6.0.1 were used.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: Our previous work (98) generated reference models using generalized additive models of location scale and shape to map neuroanatomical developmental trajectories across the life span, using a sample of 75,241 TD individuals, for total GMV, subcortical GMV (sGMV), white matter volume (WMV), ventricular volume, total SA, mean CT, regional CT, regional cortical volume (CV), and regional SA; Regional estimates of each cortical measure were extracted based on the Desikan-Killiany atlas; T1 images from each dataset were processed using FreeSurfer, version 6.0.1.

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: The GAMLSS normative models included age, sex (sex-stratified approach), preprocessing pipeline, and study/site as explanatory variables for model fitting. Euler number was included as a covariate in all downstream statistical analyses to account for image quality differences. ComBat harmonization was applied with covariates of age, sex, and diagnosis to preserve biological variation while controlling for site effects.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: Adopting a sex-stratified approach, the GAMLSS model included age, preprocessing pipeline, and study in estimating firstorder (μ) and second-order (σ) distribution parameters; effects of age, sex, and site/scanner; All analyses included Euler number as a covariate, as well as age, to account for potential systematic age deviations in clinical groups; ComBat was applied to the entire dataset across all global and regional measures, with each site treated as a batch and with covariates of age, sex, and diagnosis to preserve related biological variation.
